question: Does the retained FiveK freeze contain enough exact paired RAW/Expert-C support and camera-model connectivity to test a bounded explicit neutral-base parameter predictor without teaching film identity or final RGB?

source.name: MIT-Adobe FiveK retained freeze v1
source.rights_scope: internal research under the existing FiveK project boundary; no redistribution

allowed: fit bounded explicit neutral-base parameters to paired RAW/Expert-C observations
predict only bounded explicit neutral-base parameters from low-dimensional source statistics
compare identity, global, nearest-neighbour and ridge parameter predictors
apply a separately frozen fixed film-look operator only after neutral-base evaluation passes
forbidden: call Expert C film, stock or scanner ground truth
train a network or model that directly emits final RGB
fit or alter AO6 or any stock-look parameters
split by individual image while leaking a camera-model group
use semantic, CLIP, face, object or scene labels as the neutral-base predictor
claim calibrated, stock-specific or unpaired digital-to-film identification
delete or redistribute retained source pixels
claim_ceiling: exact internal paired-digital-retouch source and camera-group feasibility for a bounded neutral photographic base experiment; no film, stock, calibration, preference, product or final-RGB-learning claim
